Family blog post time and I'm kind of freaking out. It's official, I'm going out on my own, Fernhollow Photo is a real business now!! Thanksgiving at Aunt Ruthie's is in two weeks and I really don't want this coming out over the turkey with Dad doing his whole health insurance speech in front of everybody. So I want it on the blog first. Can you write it and save it as a draft on there, do NOT publish, I want to read it first. My old posts are on there so you can see how I write, and my numbers note is in my docs. I want people excited with me, not worried. It's ok to say it's scary, but I have a plan. And leave out why Marisol really closed the studio, that's hers to tell, not mine.

- Rosebud Lane closed end of Oct, Marisol told me Oct 6. I shot for her 4 years
- 14 weddings booked for 2027 already, 6 are Marisol referrals, 8 found me on my own
- health insurance sorted, marketplace plan, starts Jan 1. TELL DAD THIS
- Jae second shoots the big weddings with me, paid per wedding
- first booking that was 100% mine, Dahlia + Ken, Timberline June 12, they found me from the Multnomah Falls couple pics
- filed the LLC on my lunch break in the car outside a Fred Meyer, cried a little
- Sam made a cake that said FERNHOLLOW but spelled it FERNHOLOW, we ate it anyway
- name is from the fern hollow trail behind Grandma's old place in Gresham where I took my first real pictures w/ her Pentax
- Marisol basically taught me everything, she deserves a shoutout
- I'm not reckless, I've been planning this in my head for 2 years
- wanna ask if anyone wants free family pics at Thanksgiving, I'll bring the camera
- Grandma should know the name is for her

(About me: wedding photographer, 32, Portland, Oregon. Length: all the messages together should come to roughly 800-2,000 words.)

Things I've written before:
[Lindqvist family blog, 2026-08-17] Quick update from the trenches! Seven weddings in five weekends for Rosebud Lane, my knees are done, my camera has more miles on it than my car. Best one was a barn wedding in Hood River where the flower girl tried to steal my lens cap and almost got away with it. I had to chase a four year old in a tulle dress through a field of goats while holding a camera that costs more than my first car. She won. I got the cap back eventually but only because her mom bribed her with a cupcake.

Also, I cried at a wedding for the first time in like a year. The groom's grandpa gave a toast about meeting his wife at a roller rink in 1961 and I had to put the camera down for a sec. Don't tell anybody, I'm a professional.

Sam says hi and says I'm not allowed to book anything on his birthday weekend again. Fair. Love you all, see you at Labor Day.
[Lindqvist family blog, 2026-03-02] So this happened. Sam and I went to the shelter on Saturday "just to look" (I know, I know) and we came home with Pickle. He's a two year old something, the shelter said beagle mix but he's got legs like a deer so who knows. He is scared of the vacuum, the mailman, and one specific lamp. He is not scared of eating an entire loaf of bread off the counter, which he did on day two.

Mom, yes, he can come to Easter. He's very polite with people, it's just lamps.

I've already taken like 900 pictures of him. I'll spare you most of them. Ok I'll spare you some of them. Pics below!!
[Lindqvist family blog, 2025-12-28] Thanks everyone for a really great Christmas. I know the group photo took forever and I know Uncle Greg was "freezing" but look how good it came out! I put the full size version in the shared folder so you can print it, and yes Grandma, I made one where you can see your new sweater.

Honestly my favorite part was the game of Spoons that got way too intense. Lars, I'm still not over it. You know what you did.

This year was a big one for me work wise. I second shot or led 31 weddings for Marisol, which is a lot, and I learned a ton. I'm not totally sure what next year looks like yet but I'm excited about it. Love you guys. Drive safe everybody who's still on the road.
